tool_input.prompt:
Create ONE NEW isometric gameplay-character concept of Guarin in the requested drawing language. Use INPUT IMAGE 1 ONLY as the camera/volume guide: it is a mathematically projected orthographic proxy at 45 DEGREES ABOVE THE GROUND, 15 degrees steeper than the previous roughly 30-degree view. Use INPUT IMAGE 2 ONLY for Guarin's costume, colors and identity, NOT for its lower camera or comic-illustration finish. Redraw the character at Image 1's noticeably steeper angle. His barrel helmet remains UPRIGHT and its flat circular crown remains HORIZONTAL, appearing as a DEEP ellipse with minor/major axis ratio about 0.707. You must show substantially more crown surface than Image 2's shallow top. The camera guide takes priority for this angle. Show top surfaces of shoulders, shield rim and boots with consistent foreshortening. The proxy is unfinished geometry, not the final style or an equipment redesign: interpret its volumes as the existing compact knight rather than reproducing boxy forms.
Keep the existing SAME COSTUME: full-face dull iron cylindrical greathelm with flat top, two plain vertical riveted strips, narrow BLACK visor slit and small round breathing holes; NO visible eyes, skin or face; RING-mail shirt and sleeves, ragged dark wine-red scarf/short cape and waist cloth, brown belt with a plain rectangular buckle, brown gloves, taupe/brown forearm and shin wraps, short rounded brown boots. Sword in the viewer-left hand points down diagonally across the front toward the lower-right: disk pommel, straight crossguard, centered point and a rigidly straight double-edged blade. Wooden elongated kite shield on the viewer-right, dull iron rim and one narrow faded wine-red panel. Keep these items and their colors identical in all directions. The head is huge, with a tiny broad body, very short stubby limbs and wide little feet: about 2.2 helmet/head heights overall, SHORT AND SQUAT, cute, stocky and cartoony, never realistic adult anatomy or a tall slim knight. Preserve the sense of a weary adult beneath this lovable shape. The setting is the Royans/Isere lands in the 1101 story; the greathelm is the explicit user-approved exception. Do not add foreign royal ornament, emblems, plate body armor, scale cuirasses, new garments or different weapons.
Draw the actual visual language of a playable VIDEO GAME CHARACTER viewed in a dark isometric world, not a polished comic-book page, inked portrait or editorial illustration. Prioritize silhouette and material/light grouping that remain readable at gameplay size: economical ring-mail signs, large coherent cloth folds, a crisp contour and deliberately simplified faceplate. Single full body in a neutral wide-footed idle stance, facing diagonally lower-right; all boots and sword/shield tips visible, one quiet ground shadow, generous margins, flat charcoal backdrop. Hold the subdued iron gray, taupe/brown and dried-wine palette. Tiny fine pixel-shaped clusters and economical edge steps are welcome; avoid a coarse block mosaic, decorative crosshatching, manga/comic outlines, engraving, penciled marks, dense mail microtexture, captions, UI, additional views, logos or copied game characters.

A — DIABLO II LED GAME RENDERING: Make the underlying rendering feel like a carefully lit, pre-rendered dark action-RPG character sprite from Diablo II, adapted into this VERY CUTE SHORT SQUAT silhouette. Build sculptural iron and leather from restrained shaded planes, broad low-key highlights and deep occlusion, with gritty but economical material color clusters and fine raster-like edges. Rich dimensional material weight and atmospheric shadow, not line-art fills or comic ink. A dark muted game-sprite finish with compact chunky toy-like anatomy but worn matte real materials: no shiny plastic toy, no heroic realistic proportions, no painterly illustration wash. DII governs shading, material grouping and restrained gritty texture ONLY; the enormous full-face greathelm and short stubby body remain cute and cartoony. Retain the guide's 45-degree elevated view.
